item.title: Coherence protection of a silicon hole spin qubit with phase-modulated microwave driving
item.description:
Pay dirt new method — Phase-modulated concatenated continuous driving (CCD) stabilizes Rabi oscillations and extends oscillation decay time for silicon hole spin qubits while maintaining coherent gate control.

Grade 0.528 · 3.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “Silicon quantum electronics” · Sayyid I. Ibad, Yusuke Sato, Takuma Kuno, Itaru Yanagi, Toshiyuki Mine, Ryuta Tsuchiya, Digh Hisamoto, Hiroyuki Mizuno, Raisei Mizokuchi, Jun Yoneda, Tetsuo Kodera

Asks

Can low-frequency charge and hyperfine noise in silicon hole spin qubits be suppressed during coherent driving via microwave phase modulation?

But

Subject to low-frequency noise from intrinsic spin-orbit coupling and residual nuclear spins in the silicon substrate.

Tools

silicon quantum dot hole spin qubit · phase-modulated concatenated continuous driving (CCD) · microwave phase modulation · all-electrical spin-orbit control

Abstract

Hole spins in silicon quantum dots are a promising platform for quantum computing due to their strong intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which enables fast, all-electrical control. However, this coupling also increases their susceptibility to charge noise, thereby limiting coherence times. Moreover, holes in silicon are also affected by hyperfine interactions with residual nuclear spins in the silicon substrate, introducing a non-negligible source of low-frequency noise. Here, we implement a phase-modulated concatenated continuous driving (CCD) technique for hole spin qubits to suppress low-frequency noise through microwave phase modulation. This approach stabilizes Rabi oscillations and extends the oscillation decay time compared to the conventional method. Furthermore, by defining a qubit in the CCD frame, we achieve coherent control while simultaneously protecting the qubit from noise, confirming coherence protection during gate operations. These results demonstrate a viable route toward noise-robust hole spin qubits.

item.title: Superconducting qubit based on altermagnets
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Superconductor-altermagnet-superconductor junctions engineered into the 2ϕ-junction regime provide intrinsic charge-noise protection via qubit wavefunction parity while retaining large anharmonicity from coherent double-Cooper-pair tunneling.

Grade 0.465 · 2.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Xue-Feng Pan, Xin-Lei Hei, Franco Nori, Peng-Bo Li

Figure

Transition frequency, anharmonicity, transverse charge-noise coupling strength 𝒩DCQ, and longitudinal flux-noise coupling strength 𝒩DPFlux plotted versus external flux ϕext and harmonic ratio η.

Asks

Can altermagnetic Josephson junctions realize programmable non-sinusoidal current-phase relations that combine high coherence with strong anharmonicity in superconducting qubits?

Before

Unconventional d-wave superconducting qubits such as flowermon and d-mon enhance anharmonicity via higher CPR harmonics, but operate in the ϕ-junction regime and suffer from quasiparticle and charge noise.

But

Short-junction limit (L≪ξ0); symmetric junction design for the flux-tunable SQUID; single- and double-Cooper-pair harmonics retained.

Tools

Furusaki-Tsukada formula · Andreev bound state model · superconductor-altermagnet-superconductor trilayer · SQUID-based transmon architecture

Abstract

Altermagnets, characterized by vanishing net magnetization and momentum-dependent spin splitting, provide a promising platform for next-generation Josephson devices. Here, we exploit the Josephson effect in superconductor-altermagnet-superconductor junctions and show how to engineer prescribed current-phase relations by device design. Based on these programmable Josephson potentials utilizing altermagnetism, we propose a new class of transmon-like superconducting qubits that combine large anharmonicity with enhanced robustness against decoherence via coherent two-Cooper-pair tunneling. We show that in the 2φ-junction regime, this kind of qubit provides intrinsic protection against charge noise due to parity protection. Magnetic flux can be used to precisely control the qubit and, under appropriate bias, this architecture further suppresses charge and flux noise. Our results establish altermagnets as a versatile platform for Josephson-potential engineering and open a new route toward high-performance superconducting qubits combining high coherence, large anharmonicity, and broad tunability.

item.title: Deterministic synthesis and processing of frequency-bin qubits in a macroscopically coherent quantum memory
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Cavity-assisted quantum memory using pre-created long-lived macroscopic spin coherence synthesizes and stores arbitrary frequency-bin photonic qubits using only RF rotations via spectrally nonlocal impedance matching.

Grade 0.464 · 2.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Circuit quantum electrodynamics” · S. A. Moiseev

Figure

Panel (a) shows the 5-level rare-earth ion level scheme and the optical/RF pulse timing sequence. Panel (b) shows the crystal inside a dual-mode optical resonator controlled by an RF coil.

Asks

Can pre-created long-lived macroscopic spin coherence in a cavity-assisted quantum memory be used to deterministically synthesize, store, and process arbitrary frequency-bin photonic states without optical pulse shaping?

Before

Extends the single-spin-coherence PLMC protocol (Moiseev 2024), which required optical controls and stored only single-frequency photonic states.

But

Spectral width of input pulse must be much smaller than inhomogeneous absorption linewidth and cavity linewidth (δωs≪Δin,κ2,3); requires strongly correlated inhomogeneous optical broadening and negligible ground-state spin dephasing during the protocol.

Tools

Pre-created Long-lived Macroscopic (PLM) spin coherence · Dual-mode optical cavity · Rare-earth-ion-doped crystals · Spectrally nonlocal impedance matching · Heisenberg-Langevin input-output formalism

Abstract

Quantum information processing requires efficient storage and manipulation of photonic states.Here, we advance a cavity-assisted quantum memory protocol based on Pre-created Long-lived Macroscopic (PLM) coherence, thereby transforming quantum memory from a passive storage device into a platform for deterministic in-memory photonic processing. It is demonstrated that spin PLM coherence enables all-optical control of quantum memory using robust radio-frequency rotations alone. Here, the spin coherence serves as a distributed coherent quantum bus, which mediates the deterministic synthesis and storage of frequency-bin states through spectrally nonlocal impedance matching. We identify an inherent time-reversal symmetry in the underlying dynamical equations, ensuring unitary evolution of the quantum memory operations. The presented results demonstrate a unified platform for quantum storage and optical signal processing, enabling controlled manipulation of frequency-bin photonic qubits and paving the way for scalable multimode quantum networks based on spectral-encoding architectures.

item.title: Nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations in two-photon-driven nonlinear quantum optical systems
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Two-photon driving strongly enhances the drive input energy current and signal-to-noise ratio via multiphoton resonances ωd(m)≃ω0+(2m−1)U, substantially modifying non-Gaussian higher-order current cumulants compared to single-photon driving.

Grade 0.427 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Y. T. Chen, Y. W. Lu, J. C. Lu, C. Wang

Figure

Drive input energy current log10⁡(JP), second-order fluctuations log10⁡(Jl(2)), and signal-to-noise ratio 𝒮l versus drive frequency ωd, showing enhancement when two-photon loss is added to single-photon dissipation.

Asks

How two-photon driving reorganizes nonlinear dressed-state transitions to control nonequilibrium average energy current and higher-order current fluctuations in open quantum optical systems.

But

Weak-driving regime, low-energy three-state approximation, Ohmic spectral density.

Tools

rotating-frame driven quantum master equation · full counting statistics · dressed-state eigenbasis expansion

Abstract

Understanding nonequilibrium transport and fluctuations driven by nonclassical light in nonlinear quantum optical systems is challenging. Here, we formulate a driven quantum master equation in the rotating frame combined with full counting statistics, retaining the drive-induced frequency shifts in the system-reservoir interactions and providing a unified description of drive-assisted incoherent transitions based on the rotated system dressed-basis. Applied to a Kerr resonator and a nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model, the approach reveals pronounced multiphoton-resonant enhancement of the drive input energy current, with significant high peaks under two-photon driving compared to the single-photon case. The two-photon resonance relations are analytically obtained. Resonance structure in the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model nonlinearly relies on qubit-photon couplings, with additional dressed-state branches. A low-energy-state approximation attributes the resonant current enhancement to dressed-state hybridization and efficient activation of incoherent energy exchange processes. Beyond the average current, two-photon-driving induced energy exchange picture near resonance also substantially modifies the second-order current fluctuation and higher-order current cumulant, while increasing the time-normalized signal-to-noise ratio. Adding two-photon loss introduces extra incoherent photon-pair exchange pathways and further reshapes the current and its fluctuations. We hope these results may deepen interpretation of photon driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively governing nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations.

item.title: Extracting Electromagnetic Bare Mode Couplings in Large Superconducting Quantum Processors
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Avoided-crossing, energy participation ratio (EPR), induced electromotive force (EMF), and impedance-matrix methods extract transmon-to-package bare mode couplings with relative deviation under 5%.

Grade 0.424 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity quantum electrodynamics for superconducting electrical circuits: An arch…” · Reza Molavi, Ebrahim Forati, Yaxing Zhang, Andrey R. Klots, Juan Atalaya, Brandon W. Langley, Dogan A. Timucin, Moein Nazari, Ghazi Khan, Zlatko K. Minev, Alexander N. Korotkov, Michel H. Devoret

Figure

Coupling strength g/2arπ between individual transmons and the fundamental package mode across 25 array positions, comparing avoided crossing, EPR, induced EMF, and impedance matrix techniques.

Asks

How can weak electromagnetic couplings between localized transmon qubits and distributed package modes be accurately and efficiently extracted in multi-scale superconducting processor simulations?

But

Numerical full-wave simulations; transmons modeled as linear LC resonators under the rotating-wave approximation; assumes weak coupling to bare modes.

Tools

3D electromagnetic solvers · Energy participation ratio (EPR) · Induced EMF method · Impedance matrix synthesis · Avoided-level-crossing analysis

Abstract

High-fidelity control of superconducting quantum processors requires accurate characterization of electromagnetic coupling strengths among the device's constituent elements. Accurately extracting these couplings across large-scale architectures, presently featuring hundreds of qubits, poses a challenging multi-scale modeling problem. This requires resolving scales from the nanometer-scale geometry of Josephson junctions and their leads to the centimeter-scale size of the enclosing metallic packages. We present four numerical coupling extraction methods based on the avoided level crossing, the energy participation ratio, the induced electromotive force, and the impedance matrix. These methods are tailored to work with commercially available 3D electromagnetic solvers. We benchmark these techniques on a 10×10 array of transmon qubits, extracting their couplings to standing package modes. Our results show that these methods yield consistent coupling strengths with a maximum relative difference of less than 5%.

item.title: Performance optimization of cascaded traveling wave Josephson parametric amplifiers
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Cascading a 736-element SNAIL-based TWPA and a 1632-element TWPA achieves nearly 30 dB total gain over ~1 GHz bandwidth, with added noise near (1/2)ℏω and a 1 dB compression point of -101 dBm.

Grade 0.423 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity quantum electrodynamics for superconducting electrical circuits: An arch…” · Ilari Lilja, Ekaterina Mukhanova, Stanislav Khaldeev, Ilya Golokolenov, Visa Vesterinen, Pertti Hakonen

Figure

Gain versus frequency for individual and simultaneous TWPA operation, gain saturation versus pump power, and gain compression alongside signal-to-noise ratio improvement as a function of probe power at 5.503 GHz.

Asks

Can low added noise and high gain be achieved simultaneously by cascading two TWPAs, with the first optimized for minimum added noise and the second for high gain?

Before

was around 20 dB gain in single TWPAs with comparable noise and compression

But

Requires interstage bandpass filtering to prevent wideband amplified quantum noise and idler tones from saturating the second amplifier stage; gain ripples persist from imperfect interstage impedance matching.

Tools

SNAIL-based traveling-wave parametric amplifiers · interstage 5–6 GHz bandpass filter · Y-factor method calibration stage · dilution refrigerator

Abstract

Traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) based on Josephson metamaterials provide broadband gain with near-quantum-limited added noise. Whereas long nonlinear metamaterial devices can deliver high gain, short arrays suffer less from dissipation, pump depletion, and internal standing waves which can degrade noise performance. Here, we demonstrate a cascaded TWPA architecture that combines the advantages of both approaches by employing a short (736-element), low-dissipation Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL)-based TWPA as the first amplification stage, followed by a conventional long (1632-element) TWPA that provides additional gain. The resulting amplifier cascade achieves nearly 30 dB of total gain over a tunable bandwidth of approximately 1 GHz while maintaining added noise close to the quantum limit. Our results establish a cascade of TWPAs as a practical approach for high-gain, broadband, quantum amplification with applications in quantum information processing, multi-mode entanglement, and quantum sensing applications at microwave frequencies.

item.title: The Superconducting Talbot Effect in Phased-Array Josephson Junctions
item.description:
Worth a look theory — Proximitized Cooper pairs from periodic superconducting leads produce a real-space Talbot carpet repeating at ZT=λp/(1−1−λp2/d2), steerable via inter-lead phase differences Δϕ to extract Fermi wavelengths with sub-9% fitting error.

Grade 0.422 · 1.9σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Hechen Ren, Ziying Li

Figure

Real-space induced superconducting order parameter showing Talbot self-imaging at integer ZT and inverted patterns at half-integer ZT for helical and spin-degenerate 2DEGs, with corresponding critical-current oscillations versus pair wavelength λp.

Asks

Can macroscopic quantum near-field diffraction occur for proximitized Cooper pairs in a ballistic 2DEG, and can active phase control map its Fermi surface?

But

Ballistic 2DEG regime; requires sub-wavelength lithographic pitch (d∼200 nm) and planar junction lengths L≲1μm due to r−2 power-law decay of induced order parameter.

Tools

phased-array Josephson junctions · Vernier-scale collector arrays · Kwant tight-binding BdG simulations · Green's function Cooper-pair propagator model

Abstract

We introduce the superconducting Talbot effect---a macroscopic quantum self-imaging phenomenon occurring when proximitized Cooper pairs propagate through a ballistic two-dimensional electron gas. By configuring periodic superconducting leads into a phased-array Josephson junction with programmable phase differences, we demonstrate active steering of the resulting superconducting Talbot carpet. To overcome transport resolution limits, we design a Vernier-scale collector array that performs sub-wavelength sampling of the fractional Talbot pattern. This approach maps real-space quantum interference with high robustness to disorder, enabling direct extraction of Fermi wavelengths across helical, spin-degenerate, and spin-orbit-split Fermi surfaces. Tight-binding numerical calculations on a square lattice validate the real-space interference patterns. Our results establish a versatile framework for coherent wavefront engineering and quantum materials diagnostics in superconducting optics.

To overcome transport resolution limits, we design a Vernier-scale collector array that performs sub-wavelength sampling of the fractional Talbot pattern. This approach maps real-space quantum interference with high robustness to disorder, enabling direct extraction of Fermi wavelengths across helical, spin-degenerate, and spin-orbit-split Fermi surfaces. Tight-binding numerical calculations on a square lattice validate the real-space interference patterns. Our results establish a versatile framework for coherent wavefront engineering and quantum materials diagnostics in superconducting optics.

item.title: Observation of Kondo Effect in Rhombohedral Graphene Superlattices
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Kondo effect observed in hexalayer rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices. With increasing magnetic field, longitudinal magnetoresistance transitions from increasing to decreasing across critical field Bc, while Hall resistance Rxy reverses sign near Bc; longitudinal resistance Rxx increases logarithmically as temperature decreases before transitioning to a T2 heavy-fermion liquid behavior.

Grade 0.412 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Xin Liao, Qing Yin, Huiwen Wang, Jing-Wei Dong, Jun-Xi Chen, Si-Li Wu, Cai-Zhen Li, Guowei Lyu, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wei Jiang, Yu-Gui Yao, Zhi-Min Liao

Asks

Can the Kondo effect be realized and tuned via topological flat bands in rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices?

But

Observed in hexalayer rhombohedral graphene moiré structures under low temperatures and external magnetic and displacement fields.

Tools

hexalayer rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattice · magneto-transport measurements · temperature-dependent transport measurements · electrostatic gating (carrier density n and displacement field D tuning)

Abstract

Kondo effect in strongly correlated systems arises from the antiferromagnetic coupling between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, giving rise to a variety of exotic quantum phenomena. Two-dimensional moiré superlattice systems provide a highly tunable platform featuring topological flat bands, where Wannier orbitals are spatially confined by the periodic moiré potential and serve as localized magnetic moments, enabling the observable Kondo effect. Here we experimentally demonstrate Kondo interactions in hexalayer rhombohedral graphene moiré superlattices through magneto-transport and temperature-dependent measurements. With increasing magnetic field, the magnetoresistance exhibits an increase-decrease transition across a critical field B_c, while the Hall resistance R_xy undergoes a sign reversal near B_c. Moreover, as temperature decreases, the longitudinal resistance R_xx first increases logarithmically and then decreases following a T^2 behavior, indicating a transition to heavy fermion liquid. These behaviors can be consistently explained by the breakdown of Kondo singlets induced by either magnetic field or temperature, which liberates carriers previously bound to localized moments, thereby enhancing conductivity and altering the dominant carrier type. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the Kondo interaction can be continuously tuned by both carrier density n and displacement electric field D, and suggest the emergence of a Kondo insulating state. Our findings provide deep insight into the Kondo effect in moiré engineered flat-band systems, paving the path for exploring exotic correlated quantum phases.
